answer: Progressive Resource Decay Routing Agents broadcast transactions through a shared network resembling a dense garden, where each active identity increases local routing congestion. The protocol enforces an escalating bandwidth tax per concurrent identity based on local node density. For an attacker spawning thousands of sybils, this creates a steep exponential cost curve: each duplicate drains operational throughput until the swarm becomes a hollow shell unable to process state updates faster than a single comet impact on its liquidity pool.
